newsitem.title: IRAN: Iraqi opposition says U.S. attacks "inadequate".
newsitem.headline: Iraqi opposition says U.S. attacks "inadequate".

text.p: The leader of an Iranian-based Iraqi opposition group dismissed Tuesday's U.S. missile attack on Iraq as inadequate.

"The American attack is not adequate and does not match the barbaric acts committed by the army of (Iraqi President) Saddam (Hussein) when it entered northern Iraq," said Mohammad Baqir al-Hakim, head of the Supreme Council for the Islamic Revolution in Iraq (SCIRI), the main Shi'ite Moslem opposition group.

"Today's strike also does not match the challenge directed by Saddam against America and its allies by attacking areas of northern Iraq annouced as 'safe havens' by them," Hakim, speaking through an interpreter, told Reuters by telephone.

He was referring to the 27-missile U.S. blitz on military targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for an offensive by Baghdad against areas of northern Iraq which were declared as "safe havens" for Kurds after the 1991 Gulf War.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), which was pushed out of the northern city of Arbil by Baghdad's forces, said on Monday Iraqi troops were carrying out mass executions there.

SCIRI, usually active in southern Iraq, said in November it had sent some of its forces into Kurdish-run northern Iraq as part of a joint effort with the PUK to bring about the downfall of Saddam's government.
